header_changes_needed: statemgr.h: StateMgrT's +0x08 is a sead::Buffer<sead::FixedSafeString<24>>, i.e. {s32 count; FixedSafeString<24>* ptr;}, not `u32 mNames[2]`. Evidence: 0x10BEC4 (setStateName) reads [r0+8] as the count and [r0+0xC] as the base and strides by 0x24; 0x18FCA8-0x18FCA8 region of the ctor stores 8 at 0x4A4 and the new[] result at 0x4A8. Layout and size are unchanged, so existing users are unaffected; only constructors that *fill* the names need the Buffer form.

statemgr.h: StateMgrT has no setStateName declaration. The ctor calls 0x10BEC4 eight times with (this=&mStateMgr, idx, &sead::SafeString("cState_...")). Adding `void setStateName(s32 idx, const sead::SafeString& name);` would let constructors use the shared template instead of a local copy.
albw_common.h and vec3.h both define `struct Vec3`, so a file cannot include both. Not a bug in either, just a note for constructors that want SafeString and Vec3 together.
new_types: logs/manual/H_0018FBA8/actor_types.h -- ActorBaseA/ActorBaseB/ActorBase (0x150E40, 0x40C bytes, second base at +0x320, fields m54/m2cc/m2d0/m2d7/m354/m35a/m3a0/m3a4/m3d0/m3dc/m3e0/m3e4/m3e8); Delegate (16 B, vtable ro_6F4554, member-fn pointer encoded {vtable_byte_offset, (adj<<1)|1} -- decoded from 0x6830E8); StateMgrBase (0x10A794, 0x14 B) + StateMgr (0x24 B, owner/enter/exec/exit at +0x14..+0x20); FixedSafeString24 (0x24 B, ctor 0x10BDF0); Sub438 (0x64 B, ctor 0x4EE484, fields +0x10/+0x14/+0x18/+0x22/+0x32); Obj435714 (0x435714/0x4356B4, Vec3 at +4, flag at +0x2C, 0.22f at +0x58); TypeInfoRoot (static RTTI root, guard data_007266C0, object data_007266C4); Hookshot (own members from 0x40C, full offset map).
blocker: The prologue + init-list region (0x18FBA8-0x18FC40, ~110 words) is where the match dies, and everything after it is shifted. With the original's flags (-O3 -Otime) armcc spills the incoming this/param (`push {r0, r1, r4, ...}` + `ldr r1, [sp, #0x88]`) where the original does `mov r6, r1`; it also emits the two vptr stores in the opposite order (`str r1,[r0,#0x320]` before `str r1,[r0]`) and uses `ldrd r2,r3,[fp,#8]` where the original uses `add r3,r8,#8; ldm r3,{r1,r3}` for the delegate member-function-pointer constants. Under -O2 the prologue matches exactly (`push {r4,r5,r6,r7,r8,sb,sl,fp,lr}`) but the Delegate constructors stop being inlined, which is why -O2 scores higher on word count while -O3 -Otime scores higher on similarity. Second-largest gap: the RayQuery block 0x190778-0x1908CC builds a ~0x3C-byte stack struct (fields at sp+0x00..sp+0x39, incl. two SafeStrings at sp+0x00/sp+0x0C and bytes 0xC4/1 at sp+0x38/0x39) and passes it to 0x2C2D00; I only approximated it, so ~40 words there are wrong. Third: the eight-state table is emitted as setStateName(i) followed by the three table stores for index i (0x1901DC onward), which is an unusual source order I reproduced literally but whose exact source form (unrolled loop vs. eight explicit blocks) I could not pin down; the state-7 data comes from a *separate* 16-byte constant ro_6A1740 that duplicates ro_6A16B8[0x88..0x98], which suggests the original had a second static table.
helped: The shared headers helped only indirectly. vec3.h was used unchanged and its setAdd/setSub out-of-line members reproduced 0x115C54/0x115C70 exactly, and the Player constructor (0x1DEA54) was the single most useful reference: its ActorBaseA/ActorBase skeleton, its `new (nt) X(...)` idiom and its DynamicCast pattern transferred directly, and its 0x40C-byte ActorBase size is what told me that every Hookshot field below 0x40C (m354, m3a4, m3d0, m3e8, ...) actually belongs to the base class, not to Hookshot. statemgr.h's StateMgrT layout was correct in size and in the owner/enter/exec/exit offsets, but it is missing setStateName and models the name buffer as u32[2], so I had to write a local copy. The time went almost entirely into decoding the 3.5 KB body: the function is not one constructor but a constructor plus an inlined state-machine setup plus an inlined collision-query setup, and roughly 40% of it (0x190778-0x190908) is a stack-struct build I could only approximate. One genuine finding worth recording: the original passes an *uninitialised* heap pointer to both operator new[] calls -- 0x18FD5C and 0x18FD84 are `mov r1, sl` and sl is never written before them (the only two such sites in the whole 6.4 MB binary, verified by scanning for E1A0100A followed by a bl to 0x10BA78). armcc reproduces that shape from an uninitialised `Heap*` local used twice, which is what final.cpp does; it is the original's bug, not a trick of mine, but it is worth flagging because it means the shipped game reads an indeterminate register there.
